utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody today. Can we have the appearances for today. I beg your pardon. Can we call the case first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-04-83-T number, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the room. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Aditya Menon, and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Vasvija Vidovic and Mr. Nicholas Robson on behalf of the Defence of General Delic, with our assistants, Lejla Gluhic and Asja Zujo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis. Before you start, Mr. Mundis, can I just say that we've agreed on the Bench that we will sit for one and a quarter hours, that is, from now until half past 3.00, and then take a 30-minute break, and it will go on like that; one and a quarter hours, 30 minutes' break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Sinan Begovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness read the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated, sir. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Begovic.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, sir, could you please state your name, date of birth, and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Sinan Begovic. I was born on the 9th of January, 1966.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And your place of birth, sir?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Suhi Dol, Travnik Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, to the best of your recollection, when did the war begin in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in our area, which is that of Central Bosnia, that was more or less -- I mean, these problems cropped up around April; whereas, in other places, there had been problems before that, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, in April 1992, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I was living in my village, the village of Suhi Dol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, sir, what steps, if any, the villagers of Suhi Dol took in order to defend themselves in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were in a place where there were no combat operations at all in that period. I'm not quite sure of what month this was in, but the only thing which happened was that the MUP of Travnik and the reserve police force were maintaining the relay up there on Vlasic. And the VRS forces took it from them by force, and this was all as far as fighting was concerned in that period in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Begovic, just for purposes of clarification, can you please tell the Trial Chamber what the MUP was or is?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, you've made reference to the VRS forces. Can you, again, explain what the VRS forces were?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Serbs. We called them the Serbian forces, the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were these Serb forces from Serbia or from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And, again, one last clarification. When you make reference to Vlasic, can you tell the Trial Chamber what Vlasic refers to?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: That is a mountain which is -- rises above our village, and this relay was the most salient feature on Mount Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of relay it was?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was a relay for communication purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, moving, sir, into the summer of 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt you just before you go into the summer of 1992, Mr. Mundis, and I'm sorry to do this for you, but for my own clarification: What is meant by a relay in this context?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would you like the witness to answer that, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you can, can you explain what a relay -- a communications relay is?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was both for communication and for television purposes, a relaying device through which the signal went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, would it be correct to say that there's a large antenna complex on the top of Mount Vlasic which served as this relay, this communication relay platform?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, probably something like that. It was for television and also for communications generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Moving, Mr. Begovic, to the summer of 1992, can you tell us what steps, if any, were taken at that point in time among the villagers of Suhi Dol to defend yourselves?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were not attacked. Our village was not attacked, but the other villages that were in the area surrounding Vlasic were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what steps, if any, were taken in Suhi Dol as a result of the attacks in the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were afraid for our safety, and we started to self-organise. We organised some guards initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the course of the second half of 1992, did this local guard evolve into any other type of organised unit?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: We received, from someone from Travnik, instructions, I believe, that we were supposed to make a list of all the able-bodied men and to make some sort of -- compose some sort of a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, in fact, did you create such a company among the villagers of Suhi Dol?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did form a company, but it was more on paper than in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Mr. Begovic, or tell the Trial Chamber what the Ljuta Greda Detachment was?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Ljuta Greda Detachment was formed later, comprising three companies. It was formed off three companies: The Suhi Dol, the Dub, and the Visnjevo companies. They were actually directed towards the area of Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately, when was the Ljuta Greda Detachment formed?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you give an approximation in terms of the month or month and year?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was at the end of 1992 or in the beginning of 1993. I really cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, can you explain to the Trial Chamber the geographic area known as the Han Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, up there, up to Vlasic, there were five or six villages which were purely Muslim; then down from Mehurici, there were mixed villages. There was Haman, a Muslim village, and then there was another one which was a Croat village, inhabited by Croats, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, where, if you could tell us, where is the Han Bila Valley in relation to these locations you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where is the Han Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: That is the part which I just described. So we belong to that valley, the name of which was Han Bila Valley, and it was named after the River Bila which flows through that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Returning, sir, to the Ljuta Greda Detachment, do you recall who was the commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was Munir Kadic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall for how long the Ljuta Greda Detachment was in existence?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not with precision, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did the Ljuta Greda Detachment later become incorporated into another unit?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Later, when the 306th Brigade was formed, it came to be incorporated into that brigade, the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber about the structure of the 306th Mountain Brigade, or Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was established of two or three detachments. I know that the negotiations with the view to the forming of that brigade were quite lengthy, because some wanted it and some did not want it, and there was some haggling over that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when the 306th Brigade was formed?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know the exact period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you give us --

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was certainly 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximate time period in 1993 when the 306th Brigade was formed?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, sometime around mid-year. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, who was the commander of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 306th Brigade was Commander Sipic, I think. I'm not quite sure what his last name is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if you know, where the 306th Brigade was headquartered?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The headquarters of the 306th was on Rudnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did the 306th Brigade have any battalions as part of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it should have had battalions. Yes, that must have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know how many battalions the 306th Brigade had in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know where any of the battalions of the 306th Brigade were located in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The battalions did not have a permanent place. The people would stay at their homes, and only when they were supposed to go to the front would they meet at a meeting point about which they would agree beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are you familiar, sir, with the primary school in the village of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the first half of 1993, were any military units located in the primary school in the village of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were some segments of the 306th Brigade and perhaps some sort of a command, I don't know what; and then there was a group of Arabs in the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I ask a question? What was the name of the primary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mehurici, it was also called, the Mehurici Primary School. I don't know of any other name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, how many primary schools were located in the village of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: There was just this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned a group of Arabs in the school. Do you recall, Mr. Begovic, the first time you saw any Arabs in or around the primary school in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was perhaps May or June 1992. I'm not quite sure of the exact date or the exact month, but I'm sure it was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, approximately, how many Arabs were in the school in Mehurici in May or June 1992?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Between five and ten, or perhaps not even that many. Five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Moving into the first half of 1993, Mr. Begovic, were there still Arabs in and around the school in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were still some at the school, but there was also a group near Mehurici in two or three abandoned Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll get to those Arabs in the abandoned houses in just a moment, sir, but let me ask you: With respect to the first half of 1993, do you know, approximately, how many Arabs were in the school in Mehurici in early 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't know the exact number. They were still there, but I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What were the Arabs who were in the school in Mehurici doing in late 1992 and early 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know concretely what they did at the school. I know that on a couple of instances there was a training for some persons; and thereafter, after ten or 15 days of training, they distributed weapons to some people without any obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say "training," Mr. Begovic, can you tell the Trial Chamber what type of training?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was, you know, fitness training or perhaps also some religious instruction, but there was nothing very specific in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What type of clothing did the Arabs who were in the school in Mehurici wear in late 1992 and early 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, some wore Afghan caps or suits --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and then there were also some others who were in camouflage garb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did any of the Arabs that you saw in and around the school in Mehurici in late 1992 and early 1993 carry weapons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting. It is the translation. Asked by the Prosecutor what kind of clothes they were wearing, the witness said, "Afganke," which means suits, not caps. It is a type of uniform. It is a type of attire. So I should like this question to be clarified with the witness, because this interpretation is obviously incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's return, then, Mr. Begovic, to the type of clothing that the Arabs were wearing that you saw in the Mehurici school or in the immediate area in late 1992 and 1993. What type of clothing were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what I called "Afganke," this was a loose attire with quite a loose shirt up, and in the bottom are loose pants. I hope you understood me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You also told us there were others in camouflage garb. Can you describe what you meant by "camouflage garb"?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this was camouflage attire which only started to appear at that time. Some people had bought them -- bought it themselves because we didn't have it before that. Nobody had it before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were any of the Arabs that you observed in or in the immediate vicinity of the Mehurici school in late 1992 and early 1993 carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn, then, Mr. Begovic, to what you told us was two or three abandoned Serb houses and focus our attention on that location. Can you tell the Trial Chamber when you first became aware that there were Arabs in these abandoned Serb houses?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date when I found that out, but it was quite near Mehurici, so that we were aware of that fact. But I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if it was 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps early 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, the Arabs who were in the area of Mehurici, in the school and these abandoned Serb houses that were nearby, do you know who their leader was in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the command structure was when I was down there. I didn't go to see them then, and I don't know who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there later come a time, Mr. Begovic, when you became aware of who the first emir of these Arabs in Mehurici was?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Later, when I was attached to the detachment, the emir was Abu Haris. I don't know who performed that duty before that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, have you ever heard of anyone by the name of Abu Abdel Aziz?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who is Abu Abdel Aziz?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: He was one of the first to arrive at the school. I don't know who he was, though. I don't know much about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's return, then, to the abandoned Serb houses. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where these houses were in relation to Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Those houses were close to Mehurici, perhaps 500 metres or up to one kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask if the witness could be shown the electronic version of Map 10 from the Court binder, which bears ERN number 0618-6705. For the benefit of the usher, I'm going to ask the witness to make some markings electronically, so perhaps she could get ready to assist the witness with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And while that's being done, Mr. Begovic: Did the location where the abandoned Serb houses were located have a name?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: We called it Zapode. I don't know whether it had any other name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps, if the usher could be of assistance, we actually need to go to the top of the map, please. I'm going to ask the witness to make some markings electronically. Yeah, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, do you see a map in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The usher is going to hand you an electronic pen, and I would ask you, sir, if you see on this map, if you can mark the location where the school in Mehurici is located, if you see it.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot be precise. The school is right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the letters "SK" on the map?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The building that's immediately below the letters "SK," is that the location of the school in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot be precise concerning the school location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please, if you see it, mark the location -- circle the location where the abandoned two or three Serb houses were located?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I cannot be precise, but I can draw a circle. [Marks] Approximately, around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if you could please place the number "1" next to the circle that you have just drawn, indicating the location of these abandoned Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if you could then, sir, mark, to the best of your ability, the approximate location of the school in Mehurici. And if you need to circle several of the buildings, that's fine, but if you can mark the approximate location of the school in Mehurici with a circle.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And please place the number "2" next to the circle.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, we would ask that a screen shot of this be taken. I'm not sure if this Trial Chamber wants the witness to date and sign the map. Some Chambers have a preference for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not necessary, as long as it is tendered in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would ask that that be given an exhibit number and that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no objection. Perhaps, Your Honours, we could save some time by me getting up every time I have an objection, so as not to have to do it each and every time yet again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Yes. Thank you very much. The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just for the record, Your Honours, I will note that the very sensible suggestion of Mrs. Vidovic will be applied by the Prosecution as well. In the event of silence, we will -- you can take that as no objection. We will object only if we have -- we will rise only if we have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Begovic, let's turn to the period of the first six months or seven months, actually, the period from 1 January until 31 July 1993. What military unit were you serving in during this time period?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I was with the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in this time period, the first seven months of 1993, where were you staying? Where were you living? Where were you billeted, if you will?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I lived in my home, in my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the first seven months of 1993, can you tell the Trial Chamber if you and the unit you were assigned to were engaged in any combat or combat operations?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber briefly where you were engaged in combat and against which armed force or armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: We fought the HVO. I don't know what month it was, though; perhaps May or June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, again, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, the HVO refers to the Croatian Defence Council; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Croats. I don't know how else to call that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the Croats that you were fighting, sir, were they local Croats?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the people who were at their positions. There were probably some locals. As for any foreigners, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention, sir, to the 8th of June, 1993. On that day, was the unit you were assigned to engaged in any military operations?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about a date, but I was at Percin in that particular operation. If that is the date, then that is all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximate time period, sir, to the best of your recollection, when you were at the location Percin?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. Are you asking me for a date or a time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let's start with the date. If you're not certain it was the 8th of June, 1993, can you tell us approximately when, to the best of your recollection, you were at the location Percin?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Most likely it was in June. I don't know on what date, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown the electronic version of Map 9 from the Court binder. This map bears ERN number 0618-6704. We can zoom in a little bit more. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Begovic, again, I'm going to ask if the usher can assist you with the electronic pen. And before you make any markings, I'm going to ask you if you can, on this map, draw a line from where your unit went in June 1993 to the location that you've told us is known as Percin.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Here, more or less, but there's a winding road there. [Marks] However, it was in this general direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please circle Percin, and next to the line you've drawn mark the number "1"?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, before we finish with this map, let me ask you, sir: On this day in June 1993, were you aware of the presence of any Arabs in the immediate vicinity of where your unit was located on Percin?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The rumour had it that they were to the left of us, but that's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are you familiar, sir, with the location known as Borje?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: We call it Borovi, Borje or Borovi, as it is known as in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, whether there were any Arabs in that area in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Located where, at Borje or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: There are no buildings or facilities that they could have been located in. When there was an attack, this is where HVO mortar positions were, and we just went through without stopping.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Begovic, do you remember providing a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in September 2005?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you remember, in that statement, indicating that there were Arabs to the left of the location where your unit was on Percin?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you made that statement, sir, what area were you referring to where the Arabs were located or where they were on that day?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I have this place in mind. We were told that the Arabs were moving towards Borje. Later on, we heard, when coming back from our operation, that they were in the village of Radonjici and that they spent some time there. I don't know how long, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Begovic, can you please draw a circle around the area that you have referred to as Borje?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And please place the number "2" next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, on this day in June 1993, are you aware of how the Arabs got to the location that you've just circled with the number "2"?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: They also participated in the attack. That's what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I'll get to that in just a moment, please. But if you could tell me, if you know, how the Arabs got to the location Borje or Borovi that you've circled with the number "2." Where did they come from? How did they get there?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: You mean from what direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: They came from the direction of Simulje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please circle Simulje and place the letter or the number "3" next to that location?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Simulje. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So if I understand, they went from Simulje to Borje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please draw an arrow in the direction they went if Simulje to Borje?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. This is an extremely leading question. How can the witness know that unless he was with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know their direction of movement, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I had asked you, sir, if you knew, and you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we deal with the objection first? Are you dealing with the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I am trying to deal with the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I ask - I'm not quite sure how it's done here - usually when an opposite number stands up, you sit down, in my jurisdiction. So we don't sort of stand up as if we are fighting physically.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will keep that in mind, Your Honours. In response to the question on page 19, lines 5 through 8, I asked the witness if he could tell us, if he knew; and the witness answered that question on line 11 of page 19. That was the basis for asking the witness the additional questions and asking him to make the markings on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Exactly it came from the direction of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. He's answered the question that you put forth at those lines, that they came from the direction of Simulje. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And as a result of that, I asked him to make some markings, which he started to do. He made the circle. I then asked him to draw a line, if he knew, where they went from, and that's how we got to this point with respect to the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And where did he say they were moving to? To Borje? Madam Vidovic, did you still have an objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honours. The Prosecutor put a question, asking how they arrived there. I read it as asking the witness to identify the itinerary, the road that they took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, the question that's on the screen, as I see it, is: "Where did they come from? How did they get there?" And the answer was from the witness: "You mean from what direction?" The Prosecutor said: "Yes." He says, "They came from the direction of Simulje." He made those circles, and the question was: "So if I understand, they went from Simulje to Borje; is that correct?" The witness said: "Yes." "Can you please draw an arrow in the direction they went, if Simulje to Borje"? I guess it's supposed to be "From Simulje to Borje." I'm not quite sure that's a very difficult thing to make. Once you've circled Simulje and you've circled Borje, and you say they moved from Simulje to Borje, certainly you couldn't go in any direction, except the direction of Borje. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the field in Central Bosnia, it is possible in that terrain, in general, for various reasons. I don't want to testify here, but I objected to the question because the question was how they arrived there, from one location to the other. That was the gist of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your objection is how they arrived there. I'm not -- would you like to deal with that, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My question was simply to put on the record in this exhibit, in a graphic manner, the direction that they travelled from one point to the other and not necessarily the specific route that they might have gone or past which feature or location on the map, simply to enable us, three or six or eight months from now, to make more sense out of this map in terms of an arrow indicating that they went from one place to the other. If that's not helpful, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any response to that, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can clarify that with the witness during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For purposes of the record, the objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, again, can you simply draw an arrow in the direction the Arabs went from Simulje to Borje?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you want me to draw a straight arrow. I don't know exactly how they moved about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I understand that, and that's exactly why I've asked you simply to draw a straight arrow, so that in the future we can understand the direction they went.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we didn't move the way I depicted here, in a straight line. As the madam from Defence said, Bosnia is more specific. There are winding roads. You have to go around a hill in order to reach a certain location. Therefore, we don't move in straight lines, but this was just for ease of reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Exactly. And for ease of reference, sir, I'm asking you if you could draw a similar line with arrowheads indicating the direction from Simulje to Borje.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I can draw a line, but I don't know whether they moved exactly that way. There you go. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you draw arrowheads indicating the direction that they went from one place to the other?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: An arrow like this? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Begovic, do you know or do you have information or did you observe how the Arabs got to the location Simulje, marked as number "3"?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know where the Arabs who were at Simulje on their way to Borje came from, in the sense of where they were immediately before they were at Simulje?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where they used to be. We were in Suhi Dol. They may have been at their camp down at Zapode. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you don't know if the Arabs who were at Simulje came from the location at Zapode?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So from your location, sir, at Percin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please. You spoke about Percin. How do you know that this group went from Simulje to Borje? It was a rumour, was it a rumour only, or did you have firsthand evidence of this movement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The rumour was such --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe before you go, can I just also ask the witness to make a similar arrow on the Suhi Dol-Percin line, to indicate the direction of movement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, a few moments ago - and this is reflected on page 18, lines 17 and 18 - you said, in response to a question concerning Borje: "We were told that the Arabs were moving towards Borje." Do you remember who told you that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At any point prior to your unit going to Percin, did your commander or anyone else inform you that the Arabs would be involved in operations on that day?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The rumour was that they were going to participate in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: From the location that you were at, sir, on Percin, were you able to observe Simulje? Could you see Simulje from Percin?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: In terms of altitude, it is far away. We couldn't see it. Well, we might have been able to see it, but if you mean by that whether we were able to observe anyone in particular, well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And can you see from Percin to the location Borje?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We could see Borje because this is a forest, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Begovic, do you remember being interviewed by an investigator of the Tribunal on the 14th of September, 2005?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in that statement that you provided, do you remember telling the investigator that the Mujahedin were on "our left side. Their AOR," or area of responsibility, "was Simulje"?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said then, and I say now, that they were to our left. As regards the area of responsibility, I was just a simple, ordinary soldier, so whether it was their AOR or not, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I guess, sir, what I'm trying to clear up is whether there were rumours that the Mujahedin were there or whether they were actually there. And I want to give you the opportunity to clarify that or to explain that.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: They were there. That's unequivocal. They were in action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, "They were in action," can you tell us or tell the Trial Chamber where they were in action on this day in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I said, again, that they were to the left of us, approximately in this direction which I drew in on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you refer to the number or numbers on the map when you say, "in this direction which I drew on the map," can you tell us which number or numbers you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately the numbers "3" and "2."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, during the period of June 1993, was this the only -- this day that you've told us about that you were on Percin, was this the only day, that you're aware of, of combat operations in the vicinity of Suhi Dol, Maline, and Radonjici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: After that day, the unit in which I was had no more combat operations. We spent that one night at Percin, then we descended on the next day and passed through the village of Bukovica. And we were at a hill called Kukuljika down below Bukovica, and we stayed there another three or four days on the line at our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But again, sir, my question was: The day that you were on Percin in June 1993, other than that day, other than that day, were there military operations in the vicinity of Suhi Dol, Gornje Maline, Radonjici, or was that the only occasion in June 1993 where there were such military operations?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, these were the only combat activities during that period. There was nothing else around Suhi Dol at that time. Perhaps there was some incident, but I don't know that. I can't recall any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us just a moment ago that you went down to Bukovica and stayed there three or four days. After returning from Bukovica, where did you go? Or after staying in Bukovica, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No, we just through Bukovica. Bukovica had been abandoned, the population had fled. So we passed by or through Bukovica and we were at the Kukuljika Hill for three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after being at the Kukuljika Hill for a few days, where did your unit go?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: We went back home then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And which route did you take or through which villages did you go in returning home?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: We returned home here above Radonjici and above Borje, and this way via Lazine, and in then in this direction to Suhi Dol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on the way you returned by way of Radonjici, did you observe any foreigners in that --

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: We passed by Radonjici, not through Radonjici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: As you passed by Radonjici, did you observe any foreign fighters or Arabs in the vicinity of that village on that day?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were two or three Arabs near the village. We saw them, and then later we heard stories that they would not let anyone enter the village and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, at any point in time in June 1993, did you become aware of prisoners of war being kept in the Mehurici school?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Rumour had it that there were some POWs, civilians, women, and children there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any official information about prisoners of war and civilian detainees in the school?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us when you left the 306th -- actually, before we turn to that, I would ask that the map which the witness marked with the numbers "1," "2," "3" be captured and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That will be admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 64.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just a few more questions before our first break. Did there come a time, sir, when you left the 306th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: That was around the 1st of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what did you do or where did you go, what military unit did you join, on or about the 1st of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we joined these Arabs in Mehurici. Whether the detachment had been recognised or not at that time, I don't know, but we joined them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say "we joined these Arabs," can you tell us who you were referring to when you say "we joined these Arabs"?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: There were four or five of us then, lads not from the village, but four or five of us lads who joined the Arabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber, sir, the steps, if any, that you took to go from the 306th Mountain Brigade to joining the Arabs in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as the paperwork is concerned, the papers, I took no measures at all. I did nothing about those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me. It may have slipped my mind, but why were you transferred from the 306th Brigade to the Muslim -- to the Arab detachment? Did you do so by your own will or were you ordered over there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of my own will. I wasn't transferred. I just joined them of my own volition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Would you care to explain why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at that time, I was of the view that this unit that we were part of was not really organised as properly as they should have been. They were just in their infancy, and also I was prompted by some religious reasons of mine to join this detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. When you did this of your own volition, did you ask for permission or did you just walk across?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I just simply went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And was there any reaction from your superiors within the 306th Brigade to this just walking away like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't think so. I don't think there was any. I don't know. Later, I found out that we received some sort of permit or permission, sometime later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Permission to do what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every time when we left, we didn't ask anyone; but later, we found out that this move of ours had been approved by the 306th Brigade in papers, by documentation, approving our leaving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And were you given that documentation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We were never given it. We just heard this, because we were quite nearby and the people from -- we knew the people from the 306th Brigade. We knew the people who were working in its personnel department, so we got this news -- this information from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if I could just tie up a couple of loose ends on this issue, and then we can break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Begovic, did you seek any oral authorisation from your commander to move from the 306th Mountain Brigade to the Arabs in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you ever subjected to any disciplinary action as a result of switching from the 306th Mountain Brigade to the Arabs in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you ever questioned by anyone from the military police or the security administration about switching from the 306th Mountain Brigade to the Arabs in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think this would be a proper time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will break, and we will adjourn and come back at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Begovic, shortly before the break, you told us how you came to join the El-Mujahedin Unit, or the Arabs in Mehurici, as you called it, and that there were a few others who left the 306th Mountain Brigade with you at that time. Do you recall the identities of any of those individuals who joined the Arabs in Mehurici with you from the 306th on or about the 1st of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could mention a couple of names that I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Shall I? Alija Hodzic, Zikret Causevic, Safet Sarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [In English] I have a question. [Interpretation] Witness, when you left the 306th Brigade to join Arabs' unit, as you said, you felt that you were leaving behind the Bosnian Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, in a couple of moments I'm going to show you a couple of documents. But before I do that, you told us earlier today about training in the Mehurici school, and I'd like to briefly return to that subject. When you joined the Arabs in Mehurici, where was that unit located at that point in time when you joined on or about the 1st of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Near Mehurici in Zapode [Realtime transcript read in error "Zapolje"].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this is the location you marked earlier the two or three abandoned Serb houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I see that the transcript reads "Zapolje." Could you please spell "Zapode" for the record?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Just one second. Z-a-p-o-d-e.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, at the time you joined the Arabs in Mehurici or in Zapode, what type of training, if any, was that unit conducting?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: After we had just only arrived, we had training comprising fitness training, handling weapons training, and definitely there was the religious segment of the instruction, of training. Of course, I don't mean literally training, but familiarisation with Islam, to a somewhat greater extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll return to the issue of training in greater detail later this afternoon. But for now, can you tell us, was the unit in Zapode training only members of that unit or was the training extended to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was just confined to members of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now that the witness be shown document PT1505 -- PT01505. And if we could please go to the second page of that document in the original, and that would be the second page of the document also in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, do you see this document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you see your name on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which number is next to your name, sir, on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The number "7."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you mentioned a few moments ago the names of some other individuals who left the 306th with you and joined the Arabs. Do you see their names on this list; and if you do, can you please tell us the numbers next to their names?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I see, under number 16, Zikret Causevic; under number 28, Alija Hodzic; 32, Safet Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, do you know any of the other individuals listed on this document, PT1505?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which other individuals do you know that are on this list?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Number 1. Do I have also to say the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think it's sufficient if you just give the numbers, since this document is in front of us.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: So number 1, number 3, 4, 13, 17, 18, 19, 35. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us how you know these people whose names you've recognised on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: There are some neighbours of mine among them. So we used to know each other prior to joining the unit, because these are adjacent villages. So we were neighbours, and we knew each other as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Begovic, did you know any of these people during the time period that you were in the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did not quite get your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the time period, sir, that you were in the El Mujahedin Detachment, were these people that you've just mentioned, or the numbers that you've indicated, were they in that unit with you?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that PT1505 be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, sorry. PT01505 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown what was previously marked PT01538. 1538. Similarly, I would ask that we go to page 2 in the B/C/S version and page 2 in the English version as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Begovic, do you see the document in your language on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, the same question I asked you before: Do you see your name on this list?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And which number is next to your name?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: It is number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this list seems to contain the same names as the previous list, but I'll ask you, again, individuals that you know that are listed on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's more or less the same list. So what I said a minute ago applies to this list as well in terms of the people that I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Begovic, I see a reference in the second sentence of this document that, in the English, reads: "There is a group among them who are not a member of the detachment but are currently on training with us." Do you know what that might refer to?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps it was us. It may have been us. But this is probably correspondence between the units, and we perhaps had not been given authorisation yet. But I'm not quite sure. I can't say. I never saw this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would ask that PT1538 be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PT01538 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, does the document have a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you look at the first page of the document, or perhaps if we can pull up the first page, which is the transmission of this document to a number of other units, that -- the covering page does, in fact, have a date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And who was the sender? I didn't get that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The sender of the cover page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, of the document. I see, on the English version of the last exhibit, that it is addressed to - oh, there comes a new document - but it was addressed to the 306th Brigade, so I just wondered, when was it sent and from whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The document, at the bottom of the page, both in the English and the B/C/S versions, indicates the Emir, Dr. Abu Haris, was the sender of this list, which then has the covering document from Vezir Jusufspahic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So I understand it was from the Arab detachment to the 306th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then the covering document -- on both of these documents, the covering letter is sending that list other units or up the chain of command, as well as down the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So I suppose that provides the answer to the question that you just put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Begovic, let's return to the issue of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Can you tell us, sir, how that unit, at the time you joined on or about 1 August 1993, how that unit was structured?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Your Honour, the witness said that on the 1st of August, he joined a group of Arabs. He did not mention any detachments or their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I can ask some questions to clarify that of the witness. Clearly, the document we just were looking at indicated that unit detachment on the letterhead, but I can certainly ask the witness that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, the Arabs in Mehurici that you joined --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Your learned friend is still on her feet. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it has to do with the date. The witness said that the 1st of August was when he joined the group of Arabs. This document bears a date in September, the 9th of September. It is an important difference, and I maintain that the witness mentioned no detachment, at least not in reference to the 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. I can ask the witness to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, at the time you joined the Arabs in Mehurici on or about the 1st of August, 1993, can you tell us whether that group of Arabs in Mehurici had a name?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: There was no official name, but the locals called it El Mujahed. As far as I know, there was no official title, name. The people there used to call it that way, that group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say "that group of people," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The people who were there in the camp in Zapode.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, did that unit that the locals or the people in the camp called El Mujahed, did that later have any other name?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Later on, when it got organised, although I don't know when the detachment was recognised as such, it was given the name of El Mujahed, the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the time you joined this unit, the Arabs in Mehurici or El Mujahed, can you tell us about the structure of that formation?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: When I joined the unit, first, I underwent one-month training -- well, between 30 and 40 days of it. I wasn't familiar with the structure until we went into our first operation, then we were divided into groups. Up until that time, I don't know what the structure was. I can only refer to the period that followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then -- again, I'll ask you more detail about training in a few minutes. But when you say that you weren't familiar with the structure until you first went into -- or your first operation, can you tell us approximately when that was that you became aware of the structure of that unit?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: After the training, when we were sent to Kruscica for combat action, we were then deployed into different groups. This was the first time I learned about the structure within the detachment. I don't know what month it was exactly, though, when we went to Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us, sir, that you joined on or about the 1st of August, and then went to 30 or 40 days of training. So it would be sometime at least in September, if not thereafter?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: September, shortly after the training, then there was the combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this is 1993, for the record; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, at that point in time, September 1993, can you tell us about the structure of the El Mujahedin Unit?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: There were two or three combat groups, at the most, within the unit, and some Arabs that were there. This is it, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at the time, this time we're talking about now, September 1993, approximately, how big was the overall El Mujahedin Detachment? How many people? How many men?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Up to 50 men, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Begovic, can you give an approximate breakdown as to the number of those 50 men who were from Bosnia and Herzegovina and the approximate number of men who were foreigners in the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: In that period, there were more Bosniaks than Arabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, again, August/September 1993, when you first joined the unit, do you remember any of the Bosniaks who were in that unit with you? Do you remember the names of any of them?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The names I mentioned from the list, those are the people I remember; the document we saw a little while ago on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us a little bit about -- you told us that there were two or three combat groups. How many men were in each of these two or three combat groups?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: In the initial period, ten to 15 people per combat group; later, subsequently, the combat groups had up to 20 people each, but not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who was in charge of each of these combat groups?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: They were Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Begovic, were you assigned to one of these two or three combat groups?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who was the leader of your combat group in the August/September 1993 period?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Amir Puric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, the leaders of any of the other combat groups in that time period?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Within your combat group, sir, were there Bosniaks and Arabs or foreigners?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Bosniaks were separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I take it, from that answer, there were no Arabs or foreigners in your combat group in August/September 1993.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, about the leadership of the El Mujahedin Detachment in August/September 1993, above the level of these two or three combat groups?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: The emir of the detachment, if I may call it that, at the time was Abu Haris, Dr. Abu Haris. In terms of structure, there was a military emir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the name? The interpreter did not hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, for the record --

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Vahidin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than Dr. Haris and Vahidin, do you remember any of the leaders in the El Mujahedin Detachment in this time period August/September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now the witness be shown the document PT01462.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just intervene, before you leave this topic, the witness says that the emir of the detachment was Abu Haris; and then in terms of structure, there was a military emir, Vahidin. What was Abu Haris an emir of? If the other one was a military one, what was this other one, Abu Haris?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vahidin took care of military issues; training, weapons. As for any other duties of Abu Haris, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you say he was the emir of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He was the main person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vahidin was his subordinate. I don't know if you can grasp the concept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I don't, unfortunately. I would like to know if Vahidin looked after military issues, weapons and training, what did Abu Haris look after?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please have PT1462, page 3 in both English and B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it 1462 or is it 01462?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I should indicate that the English version simply contains the translation of the headings of the document, simply because it's a list and the CLSS quite often does this in order to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, do you see your name on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Not on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we then please go to page 5 in the B/C/S version of the document, towards the bottom of the document, but we need to capture the lower half of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it now. The number 105.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, on the far right-hand column, we see dates, and it would indicate a large number of persons with the same date of entry. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Here, you mean? [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On the far right-hand side, the far right-hand column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The column with dots below certain numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it. What about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This, sir, would seem to indicate that you joined the unit on the 31st of July, 1993, rather than the 1st of August, 1993. I'm just wondering if you can comment on that.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: A day or two this way or that. I don't know about the date. The 1st or the 31st. I don't think it is that important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Begovic, you were shown this document yesterday afternoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And other than your own name, did you recognise the names of anyone else on this list?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many names you recognised?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Not exactly. Ten, fifteen, twenty maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 3 of this document in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could look down this list and indicate the numbers next to the names of the people that you know and people that served in the El Mujahedin Detachment with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe it's 31, continuing from --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: 71, 78, 86, 90, 93, 98, 102, and then there's my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, finally, the last page of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, finally, if we could go to page 2 of this document, which does have a corresponding English translation, or should. It should also be page 2. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, a few moments ago I asked you about the leadership, and you gave us some answers. Do you recognise any of the other people listed under numbers 1 through 11 on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Abu Haris; Abu Maali; number 5 [as interpreted]; number 4; again, number 5. There are some names here which are listed more than once. They were on the other list as well. Number 7; number 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I misunderstood something, but could you -- how about the person listed under number 3?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC
utterances.text: From the top? Yes, Vahidin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I would ask that PT01462 be admitted into evidence and be provided with an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PT01462 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, a remark. This document does not contain the full translation of the relevant page. It can be seen that there is a notation made by hand at page 03642917. I will clarify this with the witness later on. I will have some questions concerning this, and that's why I believe it is important to have a full translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, do I understand you to be asking for a translation of this handwritten note?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, and it should be tendered only as such, with a full translation. It might be marked for identification for the time being, pending the full translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Perhaps I'm misunderstanding what my learned colleague is referring to; but if it's the handwritten note on the current page, it is translated at the very bottom of the English, where it indicates handwritten notes. And I'm not sure if she's challenging the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we have the very bottom of the English page come up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. We couldn't see it on the screen. I omitted to see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, madam. Do you now withdraw your objection, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then PT01462 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, what is the provenance [Realtime transcript read in error "providence"] of this? Who made this overview? Where does it stem from, and what credibility does it have? For the stenographer, I said, "What is the provenance." Where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't got that information at hand. I can certainly get it at the next break; and rather than misspeak or provide inaccurate information, I would prefer to wait. If you would like to hold off on a decision on the document until I can provide that, that's fine. I can certainly have it at the next break. The first page of the document, though, is a receipt that we received in obtaining this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, that's fine. Just if you would be kind enough to inform the Chamber of the provenance of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. We'll have that information at the commencement following the next break. I would ask now that the witness be shown the photo book, which was previously marked as PT06157. And what I would propose to do is simply run through that entire exhibit and see which, if any, of those photographs the witness is able to identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
